To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Higgs bosons A, H can be discovered at high-energy photon colliders for masses up to 80% of the collider energy, in the b b and neutralinos final states.

(i) the production rates of H and A in photon–photron collisions are large and can be measured with a good statistical significance, (ii) the Higgs bosons are produced in the b b and neutralinos channels, (iii) the b b final state is characterized by a very large background, (iv) the neutralino channel is characterized by a small background and a small signal, (v) the Higgs signal can be distinguished from the background in the neutralino channel
the heavy neutral Higgs particles in the MSSM can be produced in γγ collisions at the ILC, and can be found up to masses 70–80 % of the initial collider energy, for medium values of tan β.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of Higgs bosons of the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM) at photon–photon colliders.

the production of MSSM H boson in photon–photron collisions and the prospects for the search for the MSSM Higgs particles in b b final states at the photon–photon collider at the International Linear Collider.
the production of the heavy Higgs bosons A, H of the minimal supersymmetric model (MSSM) in the γγ collisions at the future e + e − linear collider (LC) with the centre-of-mass energy of 0.5–1.5 TeV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Higgs bosons of the MSSM are within reach of the LHC and the ILC, and that the ILC will have a very good chance of discovering all Higgs particles in the MSSM.
the γ γ colliders will be able to probe a large part of the MSSM parameter space and to provide the most sensitive test of the MSSM Higgs sector.
